passages.provision_quote: Sec. 1. (a) The governing body of a school corporation or charter school shall establish a: (1) procedure for each school to prepare a catalogue of materials available in the school library; (2) procedure for each school to allow a: (A) parent or guardian of a student enrolled in the school; or (B) community member: (i) within the school district; or (ii) within the school district in which the charter school is located; to submit a request to remove material from the school library that is obscene (as described in IC 35-49-2-1) or harmful to minors (as described in IC 35-49-2-2); and (3) response and appeal procedure for each school to respond to a removal request submitted by a parent, guardian, or community member described in subdivision (2). (b) The response and appeal procedure established under subsection (a)(3) must require the governing body to review the request at the next public meeting.
passages.note: Removal follows a review, but the reviewer named is the governing body (school board) itself, not a committee of educators and parents.

Final Senate passage of a Conference Committee Report on a bill with several unrelated sections (Muncie schools, vendor-survey privacy, political neutrality, school library, harmful-to-minors criminal defenses); the Yea vote alone does not tie to the library clause.
Bill details page names Donato as Senate sponsor of HB 1447, but its visible digest text describes only the third-party vendor survey privacy provision, not the library chapter.
passages.actor_quote: Sponsored by: Sen. Stacey Donato, Sen. Jeff Raatz.

rows.reasoning: As Senate sponsor of HB 1447 (2023) and a Yea vote on its Conference Committee Report, Donato acted on a bill creating IC 20-26-5.5 (School Library), which requires a parent-or-community-member removal request to be reviewed by 'the governing body' at the next public meeting. This tracks rung 3's clause that removal follow a review, but not its clause that the reviewer be 'a review committee of educators and parents,' since the named reviewer is the governing body itself; the bill's other sections are unrelated to this clause.
